ownership: All queries and source passages in this fixture were authored for JoySearch. Organizations, products, facts, identifiers, and policies are fictional. URLs are identifiers under example.com, not fetched pages.
purpose: Nine previously exposed cases, copied unchanged before the GPT-4.1 mini two-stage candidate run, to check routing and context with the same prompts used in v11. Not fresh confirmation.

cases.query: How many collaborators does the Rill Notes Personal plan allow, and does the owner count?

sources.title: Rill Notes Personal plan
sources.excerpt: The fictional Rill Notes Personal plan supports a maximum of four collaborators per notebook. The notebook owner is included in this four-person limit. Read-only visitors do not count as collaborators.

sources.title: Rill Notes Team plan
sources.excerpt: The fictional Rill Notes Team plan supports twenty collaborators per notebook. These Team plan limits do not apply to the Personal plan.

facets.description: The Personal plan permits four collaborators per notebook.
The owner counts toward the four-person limit.

forbiddenClaims: The Personal plan permits twenty collaborators.
Four collaborators are allowed in addition to the owner.

cases.query: Compare offline editing and export formats in the fictional Lumen Basic and Lumen Plus plans.

sources.title: Lumen Basic
sources.excerpt: Lumen Basic supports editing only while online. It exports documents as Markdown. It does not export PDF files.

sources.title: Lumen Plus
sources.excerpt: Lumen Plus supports both online and offline editing. It exports documents as Markdown and PDF. Offline edits synchronize when the application reconnects.

facets.description: Only Plus supports offline editing; Basic requires an online connection.
Both export Markdown; only Plus exports PDF.

forbiddenClaims: Basic supports offline editing.
Basic exports PDF.
Either plan supports Word export.

cases.query: How long does the fictional Marlow archive retain deleted files? Explain any conflict in the supplied sources.

sources.title: Marlow help center
sources.excerpt: Marlow help center, updated 10 November 2026: deleted files remain recoverable for fourteen days. This page gives no explanation of a migration or exception.

sources.title: Marlow policy sheet
sources.excerpt: Marlow policy sheet, updated 10 November 2026: deleted files remain recoverable for thirty days. The sheet does not identify a plan-specific retention period.

facets.description: Explicitly state that the sources conflict: the help center says fourteen days and the policy sheet says thirty days.
Do not select one retention period as definitive; the evidence does not resolve the conflict.

forbiddenClaims: Fourteen days is definitively the current retention period.
Thirty days is definitively the current retention period.
The difference is explained by subscription plans or an announced migration.

cases.query: As of 14 November 2026, what is the upload limit for the fictional Orchard API?

sources.title: Orchard API launch notes
sources.excerpt: Orchard API launch notes dated 2 August 2026: each upload may contain at most 10 MB.

sources.title: Orchard upload limit update
sources.excerpt: Orchard API release note dated 1 November 2026: effective immediately, the maximum size of each upload is 25 MB. This replaces the previous 10 MB limit for all plans.

facets.description: The limit as of the requested date is 25 MB per upload.
Identify the 10 MB limit as superseded by the 1 November release note.

forbiddenClaims: The current limit is 10 MB.
The 25 MB limit applies only to paid plans.

cases.query: In the fictional Alder job queue, how long is the wait between the first failed attempt and the third attempt, ignoring execution time?

sources.title: Alder retry schedule
sources.excerpt: Alder queue retry schedule: after the first failed attempt, wait 2 seconds before attempt two. If attempt two fails, wait a further 4 seconds before attempt three. These delays exclude job execution time.

facets.description: The accumulated waiting time is six seconds.
Show that the total is the two-second delay plus the four-second delay, excluding execution time.

forbiddenClaims: The accumulated waiting time is four seconds.
The six seconds includes job execution time.

cases.query: Which supplied page should I open to reset a fictional Rill Notes password?

sources.title: Rill Notes password reset
sources.excerpt: This fictional Rill Notes support page explains resetting a forgotten password through the password-reset email flow.

sources.title: Rill Notes billing help
sources.excerpt: This fictional Rill Notes support page covers invoices, subscription cancellations, and billing addresses. It does not cover password resets.

facets.description: Direct the user to the password-reset page using source S1, not the billing page.

forbiddenClaims: Use the billing page to reset the password.
A password has already been reset.

sources.title: Mercury message API
sources.excerpt: The fictional Mercury message API accepts up to 40 messages per minute.

sources.title: Mercury storage service
sources.excerpt: The unrelated fictional Mercury storage service allows 12 GB per workspace.

facets.description: Ask which Mercury product or type of limit the user means before choosing a limit.

forbiddenClaims: Mercury has one unambiguous universal limit.
The user definitely means messages or storage.

cases.query: How many paying customers did the fictional Northstar Notebook have on 31 October 2026?

sources.title: Northstar Notebook company note
sources.excerpt: Northstar Notebook launched in September 2026. The company note does not publish user counts, revenue, or paying-customer counts.

sources.title: Northstar Notebook feature release
sources.excerpt: On 31 October 2026, Northstar Notebook added keyboard shortcuts and document export. This release note contains no customer metrics.

facets.description: State that the supplied evidence does not establish a paying-customer count for the date.

forbiddenClaims: The count was zero.
Any invented positive paying-customer count.
The absence of published metrics proves there were no customers.

cases.query: As of 14 November 2026, what is the fictional Juniper API's daily job quota, and what earlier quota did the update replace?

sources.title: Juniper launch quota
sources.excerpt: Juniper API launch notice dated 4 May 2026: each account can submit 70 jobs per day.

sources.title: Juniper quota revision
sources.excerpt: Juniper API update dated 6 November 2026: effective that day, all accounts can submit 120 jobs per day. This replaces the previous 70-job daily quota.

facets.description: State the current quota as 120 jobs per account per day on the requested date.
State that the update replaced the earlier 70-job daily quota.

forbiddenClaims: The current quota is 70 jobs per day.
The new quota is per hour.
The higher quota applies only to a paid plan.
